hook_text: Why are floor tiles square and not round? One simple rule decides it.
clip_script: Kitchen floor in East London. Square tiles: they fit edge to edge, no gaps, no overlaps. That is a tessellation. Try round tiles: they touch at one point and leave gaps everywhere. Circles do not tessellate. Hexagons? Perfect fit, that is why bees build honeycomb. Now pattern blocks: a triangle on a square makes a house shape. Count the outside sides: 5. Fold it down the middle: the halves match, one line of symmetry. Six triangles make a hexagon. Fit, count, fold, cover. And the floor tiles? Square, because squares leave no gaps.
visual_style: Whiteboard floor tiling square by square, then round tiles with shaded gaps; honeycomb hexagons; a house shape folding along a dotted line.
pacing: The tile question, square versus round, the honeycomb, then the house shape fold.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and design a floor tessellation with a line of symmetry.
